input:
The IT provider corpITOp requires a service to manage 5,000 office employees. This service must filter dangerous websites, 
scan downloaded files for malware, and ensure that sensitive data does not leave the network. The service chain includes, 
in order: a webFilterVF allocated at the edge, a malwareScannerVF located in the cloud, and a dlpEngineVF located in the cloud. 
Regarding requirements, it is a mandatory requirement that the latency from webFilterVF to the malwareScannerVF remains below 10 milliseconds. 
Furthermore, the bandwidth between the malwareScannerVF and the dlpEngineVF must be greater than 500 mbps.

The media provider cinemaRenderOp requires a service to manage 5,000 rendering projects. This infrastructure receives raw digital scenes, 
distributes the rendering computation across hundreds of virtual nodes, and reassembles the finished frames for post-production. 
The deployed service chain includes, in order: a sceneReceiverVF allocated at the edge, an assetValidatorVF located in the cloud, 
a renderDistributorVF located in the cloud, a frameAssemblerVF located in the cloud, and a colorGraderVF located in the cloud. 
Regarding requirements, compression is applied after the sceneReceiverVF. Furthermore, the provider prefers that the total chain hardware 
remains lower than 800 gb. Finally, caching is executed before the colorGraderVF.

The media provider liveSubsOp requires a live subtitling service to manage 10,000 concurrent streams. This service intercepts the audio of a 
streaming event, transforms it into text via AI, translates it into three languages, and reinserts it into the video feed as subtitles. 
The deployed service chain includes, in order: an audioExtractorVF allocated at the edge, a speechToTextVF function located in the cloud, 
a multiTranslatorVF located in the cloud, and a subtitleInjectorVF allocated at the edge. Regarding requirements, caching is applied after 
the audioExtractorVF. Furthermore, the provider prefers that the total chain hardware remains lower than 100 gb. Finally, it is strictly 
required that the latency from the speechToTextVF function to the subtitleInjectorVF remains below 20 ms.

The enterprise provider corpDocOp requires a document classification engine to manage 50,000 daily files. This system analyzes PDF files or 
OCR scans, identifies the document type like invoice, contract, or reminder, and routes it to the competent business function. 
The deployed service chain includes, in order: an ocrScannerVF allocated at the edge, a textExtractorVF located in the edge, an aiDocumentClassifierVF located in the cloud, a dataRedactorVF located in the cloud, and adocumentRouterVF located in the cloud. Regarding requirements, 
security is applied after the ocrScannerVF. Furthermore, it is a mandatory requirement that the ocrScannerVF and the textExtractorVF are deployed 
on the same hosting node. It is strictly required that the latency from the textExtractorVF to the aiDocumentClassifierVF remains below 50 ms. 
Additionally, privacy is executed before the dataRedactorVF. Finally, the provider prefers that the bandwidth from the aiDocumentClassifierVF to 
the documentRouterVF remains higher than 500 mbps.

The financial provider fraudSafeOp requires an antifraud analysis service to manage 200,000 transactions per hour. This system intercepts every digital 
payment request, compares it with habitual user spending patterns via machine learning, and authorizes the transaction in a few milliseconds. 
The deployed service chain includes, in order: a requestInterceptorVF at the edge, a profileMatcherVF at the edge, an mlAnalyzerVF in the cloud, a policyEnforcerVF 
in the cloud, and a responseEmitterVF in the cloud. Regarding requirements, security is applied after the requestInterceptorVF. Furthermore, it is strictly required 
that the requestInterceptorVF and the profileMatcherVF are deployed on the same hosting node. Privacy is executed before the mlAnalyzerVF. Finally, the provider prefers 
that the bandwidth from the mlAnalyzerVF to the policyEnforcerVF remains higher than 1000 mbps, and that the total chain hardware remains lower than 120 gb.

The financial provider hftGlobalOp requires a high frequency trading service to manage 500,000 orders. This infrastructure receives stock prices, 
executes decision algorithms, and sends purchase orders seeking the fastest network path. The deployed service chain includes, in order: a marketFeedVF allocated at the edge, a tradingAlgoVF allocated at the edge, a riskCheckerVF located in the cloud, and an orderDispatcherVF allocated at the edge. 
Regarding requirements, caching is applied after the marketFeedVF. Furthermore, it is strictly required that the latency from the marketFeedVF to the 
tradingAlgoVF remains below 50 ms. The provider prefers that the bandwidth from the tradingAlgoVF to the riskCheckerVF remains higher than 5000 mbps. 
Additionally, it is desired that the latency from the riskCheckerVF to the orderDispatcherVF remains below 5 ms. Finally, logging is executed before 
the orderDispatcherVF.

The financial provider onlineBankOp requires a digital identity verification service to manage 10,000 daily uploads. This service processes photos of 
documents uploaded by users, verifies their authenticity, and compares the data with international blacklists to prevent money laundering. 
The deployed service chain includes, in order: a documentReceiverVF allocated at the edge, an authenticityCheckerVF located in the cloud, an amlMatcherVF 
located in the cloud, and a profileCreatorVF located in the cloud. Regarding requirements, encoding is applied after the documentReceiverVF. Security is 
executed before the authenticityCheckerVF. Privacy is applied after the amlMatcherVF. Finally, compression is executed before the profileCreatorVF.

The service provider eInvoiceOp requires a digital invoicing service to manage 50,000 invoices per day. This system transforms sales data into certified XML files, 
applies the digital signature, and automatically sends them to governmental systems for fiscal validation. The deployed service chain includes, in order: a saleDataCollectorVF allocated at the edge, an xmlConverterVF located in the cloud, a digitalSignerVF located in the cloud, and a taxAuthorityTransmitterVF transmitter located in the cloud. 
Regarding requirements, the provider mandates that the total chain hardware remains lower than 150 gb. Furthermore, it is strictly required that the latency from the 
xmlConverterVF to the digitalSignerVF remains below 30 ms. Finally, the provider prefers that the bandwidth from the digitalSignerVF to the taxAuthorityTransmitterVF transmitter 
remains higher than 100 mbps.

The logistics provider deliveryLogisticsOp requires a route optimization service to manage 15,000 couriers. This software receives the GPS positions of a fleet, 
analyzes city traffic data, constantly recalculates the best route for each courier, and updates their terminals. The deployed service chain includes, in order: 
a gpsIngesterVF allocated at the edge, a trafficAnalyzerVF located in the cloud, a routeOptimizerVF located in the cloud, and a terminalUpdaterVF allocated at the edge. 
Regarding requirements, compression is applied after the gpsIngesterVF. Furthermore, decoding is executed before the terminalUpdaterVF. Finally, it is strictly required 
that the latency from the begin to the end of the chain remains below 80 ms.

The municipal provider smartParkOp requires a parking management backend to handle 100,000 active parking spots. This system receives occupancy alerts, 
updates the city map, and processes automatic payments. The service chain includes, in order: a sensorDataCollectorVF at the edge, a mapUpdaterVF in the cloud, 
a paymentProcessorVF in the cloud, a statusLoggerVF in the cloud, and a securityEnforcerVF in the cloud. Regarding requirements, compression is applied after the 
sensorDataCollectorVF. Encoding is executed before the paymentProcessorVF. Security is applied after the paymentProcessorVF. Logging is executed before the statusLoggerVF. 
Furthermore, it is mandatory that the mapUpdaterVF and the paymentProcessorVF are deployed on dedicated nodes. Finally, it is strictly 
required that the latency from the sensorDataCollectorVF to the securityEnforcerVF remains below 30 ms.

The logistics provider aeroDeliveryOp requires a drone fleet control service to manage 5,000 active delivery drones. This system manages digital 
flight plans, avoids software collisions, and ensures that the command signal is always a priority. The deployed service chain includes, in order: 
a flightTelemetryIngesterVF allocated at the edge, a collisionAvoiderVF located in the cloud, a commandPrioritizerVF located in the cloud, and a routeDispatcherVF allocated at the edge. Regarding requirements, caching is applied after the flightTelemetryIngesterVF. Furthermore, the provider prefers 
that the total chain hardware remains lower than 200 gb. It is strictly required that the latency from the flightTelemetryIngesterVF to the collisionAvoiderVF remains below 10 ms. Finally, the provider prefers that the bandwidth from the collisionAvoiderVF to the routeDispatcherVF remains higher than 2000 mbps.

The cybersecurity provider secureMailOp requires a service to manage 10,000 corporate mailboxes. This pipeline intercepts incoming emails, 
removes phishing links, analyzes attachments in an isolated environment, and delivers only safe messages to the server. The service chain includes, 
in order: a mailGatewayVF allocated at the edge, a phishingFilterVF located in the cloud, a sandboxScannerVF located in the cloud, and a safeDeliveryVF 
node located in the cloud. Regarding requirements, decoding must be applied after the mailGatewayVF. Furthermore, the provider prefers to keep the 
latency from the mailGatewayVF to the phishingFilterVF below 50 milliseconds. It is strictly required that the bandwidth from the phishingFilterVF to 
the sandboxScannerVF is higher than 100 Mbps. Finally, logging is mandatory before the sandboxScannerVF.

The infrastructure provider serverMonOp requires a telemetry monitoring service to manage 50,000 virtual machines. This service collects temperature, 
CPU load, and memory usage data, aggregating them to identify anomalies before failure occurs. The deployed service chain includes, in order: a telemetryCollectorVF at the edge, adataAggregatorVF in the edge, an anomalyDetectorVF in the cloud, and an alertDispatcherVF in the cloud. Regarding requirements, 
it is strictly required that the latency from the begin to the end of the chain remains below 100 ms. The provider prefers that the bandwidth from the 
begin to the end of the chain remains higher than 2000 mbps. Finally, it is mandatory that the telemetryCollectorVF and the dataAggregatorVF are deployed 
on the same hosting node.

The industrial provider autoWarehouseOp requires a remote control system for autonomous machines to manage 500 warehouse robots. 
This software receives sensor data, calculates paths to avoid collisions, and sends steering and braking commands. The deployed service chain includes, 
in order: a sensorDataDecoderVF allocated at the edge, a collisionPathSolverVF located in the cloud, and a commandEncoderVF allocated at the edge. 
Regarding requirements, decoding is applied after the sensorDataDecoderVF. Furthermore, it is strictly required that the latency from the sensorDataDecoderVF 
to the commandEncoderVF remains below 500 ms. Finally, encoding is executed before the commandEncoderVF.

The healthcare provider healthCareOp requires a post-operative tele-monitoring service to manage 5,000 active patients. This service receives digitalized patient vital 
data from home, analyzes cardiac anomalies, and notifies the doctor on duty immediately in case of danger. The deployed service chain includes, in order: a patientDataReceiverVF allocated at the edge, a cardiacAnomalyAnalyzerVF located in the cloud, a medicalAlertLoggerVF located in the cloud, and a doctorNotifierVF located 
in the cloud. Regarding requirements, privacy is applied after the patientDataReceiverVF. Furthermore, logging is executed before the medicalAlertLoggerVF. 
It is strictly required that the latency from the patientDataReceiverVF to the doctorNotifierVF remains below 100 ms. Finally, the provider prefers that the 
total chain hardware remains lower than 80 gb.

The healthcare provider medDiagnosticOp requires a radiology AI diagnostics service to manage 10,000 daily scans. This pipeline receives high-resolution 
medical images, processes them with computer vision algorithms to highlight suspicious lesions, and stores them securely. The deployed service chain includes, 
in order: a dicomIngesterVF allocated at the edge, a lesionAnalyzerVF located in the cloud, a metadataExtractorVF located in the cloud, and a secureArchiverVF 
located in the cloud. Regarding operational requirements compression is applied after the dicomIngesterVF, while ensuring that the network bandwidth 
from this initial dicomIngesterVF to the lesionAnalyzerVF remains higher than 500 mbps. To guarantee maximum computing performance, it is mandatory that the 
lesionAnalyzerVF and the metadataExtractorVF are hosted on completely separate, dedicated physical servers. Finally, data encoding is executed before the secureArchiverVF for permanent storage.

The digital provider secureVoteOp requires a certified electronic voting service to manage 200,000 voters. This platform for public or corporate consultations 
guarantees vote anonymity and prevents data manipulation. The deployed service chain includes, in order: a ballotIngesterVF allocated at the edge, an anonymizerVoteVF 
located in the cloud, an integrityEnforcerVF located in the cloud, a voteCounterVF located in the cloud, and an electoralAuditLoggerVF located in the cloud. 
Regarding requirements, the provider prefers that the network bandwidth from the ballotIngesterVF to the anonymizerVoteVF remains higher than 100 mbps. 
Furthermore, user privacy is applied after the anonymizerVoteVF. Security is executed before the integrityEnforcerVF to protect the system from external manipulation. 
Finally, logging is executed before the electoralAuditLoggerVF to compile compliance history.

The digital provider govDataOp requires an open data portal service to manage 30,000 dataset downloads per day. This system extracts datasets from public databases, 
normalizes them into open formats, adds search metadata, and makes them available for public download. The deployed service chain includes, in order: 
adataExtractorVF allocated at the edge, a formatNormalizerVF located in the cloud, a metadataEnricherVF located in the cloud, 
and a downloadProviderVF located in the cloud. Regarding operational requirements, data caching is applied after the formatNormalizerVF. 
Furthermore, it is strictly required that the latency from thedataExtractorVF to the downloadProviderVF remains below 200 ms. 
The provider prefers that the network bandwidth from the formatNormalizerVF to the metadataEnricherVF remains higher than 1000 mbps. Finally, it is mandatory that the formatNormalizerVF and the metadataEnricherVF are hosted together on the exact same physical server to optimize data exchange.

The educational provider eduCloudOp requires a virtual student lab platform to support 10,000 concurrent students. This system provides 
temporary programming environments, manages resource allocation for each student, and monitors the workspaces to prevent improper use. The deployed service 
chain includes, in order: a sessionIngesterVF allocated at the edge, a resourceAllocatorVF located in the cloud, an activityMonitorVF located in the cloud, a userPrivacyEnforcerVF located in the cloud, an auditLoggerVF located in the cloud, and an outputPackagerVF located in the cloud. Regarding constraints, data privacy 
mechanisms are applied after the sessionIngesterVF. To detect anomalies early, security are executed before the activityMonitorVF, while ensuring that 
the latency time between the initial sessionIngesterVF and this resourceAllocatorVF is kept under 40 ms. Furthermore, logging operations are executed 
before the auditLoggerVF. Data compression is applied after the final outputPackagerVF. For the network backbone, the provider requires that the bandwidth between 
the sessionIngesterVF and the resourceAllocatorVF supports more than 500 mbps. Finally, the provider prefers that the aggregate infrastructure footprint stays below 120 gb.

The marketing provider sentimentOp requires a customer sentiment analysis platform to manage 100,000 daily reviews and comments. This software scans social media 
inputs, identifies prevailing emotions toward specific products, and sends weekly reports to the marketing department. The deployed service chain includes, 
in order: a social socialDataReceiverVF allocated at the edge, asentimentAnalyzerVF located in the cloud, and a reportDispatcherVF located in the cloud. Regarding 
system constraints, privacy mechanisms are applied after the social socialDataReceiverVF, while security is executed before the sentimentAnalyzerVF to 
safeguard the AI processing logic. Finally, to eliminate data transfer overhead, it is mandatory that thesentimentAnalyzerVF and the reportDispatcherVF are 
co-located on the same physical hosting node.

The industrial provider factoryCloudOp requires an augmented reality back-end service to support 500 active smart glasses on the shop floor. This service 
sends visual technical instructions to workers' headsets, overlaying maintenance data on the framed machinery in real time. The deployed service chain 
includes, in order: an arStreamReceiverVF allocated at the edge, an arPoseEstimatorVF located in the cloud, a dataOverlayEngineVF located in the cloud, 
and an arStreamDispatcherVF located in the cloud. Regarding system performance, the provider requires that the network bandwidth from the initial node to the arPoseEstimatorVF remains higher than 200 mbps. To prevent any lag in the workers' field of view, it is strictly required that the end-to-end 
latency from the arStreamReceiverVF to the final arStreamDispatcherVF remains below 12 ms. To avoid computational interference, it is mandatory that arPoseEstimatorVF and the dataOverlayEngineVF are hosted on separate, completely dedicated physical servers. Finally, the provider prefers that the total chain 
hardware remains lower than 90 gb to control operational costs.

The digital provider subscriptionOp requires a SaaS subscription management service to manage 50,000 active accounts. This recurring billing service handles 
customer payment cycles, software plan upgrades, and automated reminders for expired credit cards. The deployed service chain includes, in order: 
a subscriptionIngesterVF allocated at the edge, a billingCycleProcessorVF located in the cloud, a dunningManagerVF located in the cloud, and an invoiceGeneratorVF located in the cloud. Regarding operational requirements, customer privacy is applied after the subscriptionIngesterVF. To interpret the incoming 
API payloads safely, decoding is executed before the billingCycleProcessorVF. Furthermore, transaction logging is executed before the dunningManagerVF to 
keep historical track of payment failures. Finally, encoding is executed before the invoiceGeneratorVF to protect sensitive financial records.

The website security provider ddosProtectionOp requires an anti-DDoS defense system to handle 50,000 active web users. This system analyzes incoming traffic, 
cleans malicious flows, and ensures server availability. The deployed service chain consists of: a networkTrafficAnalyzerVF located at the edge, a scrubbingFilterVF 
located in the cloud, a rateLimiterVF located in the cloud, and a webServerVF located in the cloud. For security operations, it is mandatory that security is 
applied before the scrubbingFilterVF. Furthermore, it is strictly required that the bandwidth between the networkTrafficAnalyzerVF and the scrubbingFilterVF is greater 
than 500 megabps. Additionally, the provider prefers to enforce logging after the rateLimiterVF. Finally, it is desired that the latency from the rateLimiterVF 
to the webServerVF remains lower than 10 ms.

The software provider devToolsOp requires a code efficiency analyzer service to manage 20,000 daily evaluation requests. This platform receives code snippets, 
executes a simulated runtime execution, and suggests specific optimizations to reduce computational resource consumption. 
The deployed service chain includes, in order: a codeReceiverVF allocated at the edge, a syntaxValidatorVF located in the cloud, 
a sandboxSimulatorVF located in the cloud, an optimizationEngineVF located in the cloud, and a developersReportGeneratorVF located in the cloud. 
Regarding operational requirements, caching is applied after the syntaxValidatorVF to avoid processing identical code inputs. Furthermore, 
data compression is applied after the final developersReportGeneratorVF to streamline delivery. Finally, the provider prefers that the total chain hardware 
remains lower than 110 gb to minimize overall infrastructure overhead.

The compliance provider gdprComplianceOp requires a GDPR verification service to manage 5,000 corporate database connections. This service scans 
corporate databases to identify unprotected personal data, applies automatic anonymization, and generates reports for regulators. The deployed service 
chain includes, in order: a dbScannerVF allocated at the edge, an anonymizerVF in the cloud, and a reportGeneratorVF located in the cloud. 
Regarding requirements, privacy must be applied after the dbScannerVF. Furthermore, it is desired that the latency from the dbScannerVF to the 
anonymizerVF remains lower than 20 ms. It is strictly required that the bandwidth from the anonymizerVF to the reportGeneratorVF is higher than 50 Mbps. Finally, 
security is mandatory before the reportGeneratorVF.

The network security provider secureCryptoOp requires an encrypted traffic analysis service to support 25,000 corporate users. This service inspects HTTPS flows 
without fully decrypting them, using AI to identify malware or botnet patterns. The deployed service chain includes, in order: trafficSplitterVF allocated at 
the edge, a featureExtractorVF located in the edge, an aiClassifierVF located in the cloud, an alertManagerVF located in the cloud, and a policyEnforcerVF located 
in the cloud. Regarding requirements, decoding is applied after the trafficSplitterVF. Furthermore, the provider prefers to keep the total chain hardware lower 
than 80 gigabytes. It is mandatory that the trafficSplitterVF and the featureExtractorVF are deployed on the same hosting node. Finally, security is enforced 
before the policyEnforcerVF.

The government provider govMessagingOp requires a service to manage 50,000 institutional messages. This service receives digital communications,
verifies the electronic signature of the sender, checks its integrity, and archives the message in a legal vault. The deployed service chain 
includes, in order: a msgReceiverVF allocated at the edge, a sigVerifierVF located in the cloud, an integrityCheckerVF located in the 
cloud, and a legalVaultVF located in the cloud. Regarding requirements, caching is applied after the msgReceiverVF. Furthermore, the provider 
prefers to keep the total chain hardware lower than 100 gb. It is a mandatory requirement that the sigVerifierVF and the integrityCheckerVF 
operate on the same node. Finally, compression is applied before the legalVaultVF.

The gaming provider cloudGamingOp requires a service to manage 40,000 active gamers. This service executes video games on powerful servers 
and sends the video stream to the user, guaranteeing a very low latency to avoid making the game unplayable. The deployed service chain 
includes, in order: a gameExecutorVF allocated in the cloud, a streamPackerVF allocated in the cloud, and a deliveryOptimizerVF allocated 
at the edge. Regarding requirements, encoding is applied after the gameExecutorVF. Furthermore, it is strictly required that the latency 
from the streamPackerVF to the deliveryOptimizerVF remains below 30 ms. Finally, the provider prefers that the gameExecutorVF and the streamPackerVF operate on dedicated nodes.

The media provider mediaBroadcastOp requires a live multicamera streaming service to support 30,000 concurrent viewers. 
This system receives video streams from different angles, allows cloud mixing, adds advertising graphics, and distributes the signal to 
thousands of viewers simultaneously. The deployed service chain includes, in order: a streamIngesterVF allocated at the edge, a cloudStudioVF 
located in the cloud, a graphicInjectorVF located in the cloud, and a streamDistributorVF located in the cloud. Regarding requirements, 
compression is applied after the streamIngesterVF. Furthermore, it is strictly required that the bandwidth from the graphicInjectorVF to 
the streamDistributorVF remains higher than 5000 mbps. Additionally, the provider prefers that the total chain hardware is lower than 150 gb. 
Finally, caching is executed before the streamDistributorVF.

The media provider vodStreamOp requires a video on demand distribution service to manage 80,000 active subscribers. 
This service optimizes movie delivery by encrypting content with DRM, compressing it into different formats, and storing it on 
nodes close to the user to avoid buffering. The deployed service chain includes, in order: a drmEncryptorVF allocated in the cloud, 
a transcoderVF allocated in the cloud, and a cachingNodeVF node allocated at the edge. Regarding requirements, encoding is applied after 
the drmEncryptorVF. Furthermore, it is strictly required that the bandwidth from the transcoderVF to the cachingNodeVF 
node remains higher than 10000 mbps. Finally, the provider prefers that the drmEncryptorVF and the transcoderVF operate on the same node, 
while decoding is applied before the cachingNodeVF node.
